source.title: Sparse Internal Control of Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports IOI steering results using its own sparse-driver interventions and compares selected locations with the manual IOI circuit, but does not test the claimed 26-head circuit or its stated roles.
record.gate_note: The IOI experiments measure task-readout changes under sparse activation interventions, not whether the original circuit is necessary or whether its named head classes play their proposed roles. The paper's backup experiment adds candidates to a selected site; it does not ablate the main name-mover heads. Rows below record IOI outcomes that do not test any listed claim version. Results for other tasks are outside this claim. Figure 2 also shows qualitative IOI dose and KL curves; no numerical values for those curves are stated, so they are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: IOI on GPT-2 small is used only as a benchmark task for a steering framework. The paper fits additive sparse interventions at head-position sites and scores its own selectors on reachability, reversal, dose, feedback and reuse. It never ablates or patches the Wang et al. circuit, its head classes or the name-mover heads. It does not vary circuit-evaluation choices and reports no IOI results by prompt variant. The recurrence analysis only says the selected sites 'can be compared with the manual IOI circuit'; no comparison is reported. The 'backup' label in Figure G.1 is a recurrence band, not self-repair under ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors conclude that sparse internal interventions can steer task-defined readouts (IOI, MCQA, Sentiment, Refusal). They find reachability depends strongly on evaluation-pair direction information. Recovery, reversal, dose response, feedback, preservation and reuse are distinct properties. The paper does not say its IOI results bear on, or fail to establish, the Wang et al. circuit; that framing is the reader's, not the authors'.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse-driver selection and additive inference-time activation interventions, rather than the original study's circuit-discovery and circuit-ablation/patching procedure; it does not test the original 26-head circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: The IOI series use different panels and measures; nominal reconstruction uses evaluation-pair directions on the same fitting/evaluation panel, while held-out reuse retains evaluation-pair directions. The paper does not report an IOI result stratified by ABBA versus BABA template.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 25 seed-budget configurations, the sparse selector most often picks L9.END.H9 and L10.END.H7, each in 15/25. These heads overlap with name-mover and negative-name-mover heads in the original circuit, but the paper reports no comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-based sparse driver selection for IOI steering recurrently selects late END-position heads that coincide with heads in the manual IOI circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse additive head-position interventions reconstruct IOI clean-corrupt logit-margin displacements on the fitting panel. Driver-OMP gives Reltar 0.201 and random supports 0.747.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse internal activation interventions can recover IOI readouts on GPT-2 small in a paired-prompt setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out IOI recovery with the selected sites is partial: 0.30 to 0.63, against a random-support value of about -0.67.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected IOI intervention sites transfer only partially to held-out prompts.

record.problems: The IOI nominal reconstruction uses the same 64 pairs for fitting and evaluation. IOI evidence is limited to the study's particular readout, candidate library and paired prompts, and does not intervene on or test the claimed circuit. The backup augmentation does not ablate the claimed main name-mover heads. Held-out IOI reuse still uses evaluation-pair directions. The paper notes that its backup error statistic differs from stacked-vector Rclean and that its random reference is not size-matched to the final support.
record.rows_left_out: No numerical IOI dose-curve values are stated in the text; Figure 2 is described qualitatively as showing graded responses, so those plotted values are not extracted. Non-IOI task results are not relevant to this claim.

untested.parts: Whole version: the 26 heads, 7 classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
Whole version: no ablation of the main name-mover heads and no measure of compensation by other heads.
Whole version: IOI is run only on GPT-2 small and no circuit is compared across models or checkpoints.
Whole version: the sparse-driver selectors are not compared to the original circuit. Recurrent sites (L9.END.H9, L10.END.H7) are noted, but no overlap is computed.
Whole version: the circuit's faithfulness and completeness are never evaluated.
Whole version: ABBA/BABA prompts are pooled and no per-template or more-names results are given.

record.verdict_notes: Study is not an original source. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']; the state fields on R04 and R12-R14 are reset because they have no claim referent. The recurrence result (G.4.1) is a selection-frequency diagnostic of the study's own method, recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a row. Relation set to cites_only: the paper cites Wang et al. and borrows its task but does not rely on or test the circuit finding.

versions.untested_parts: The claimed 26 heads, seven classes, their roles under patching, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No ablation of the main name-mover heads or test of self-repair by backup heads.
No IOI circuit comparison across models, sizes or checkpoints, and no test of component reuse for other tasks.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods or ablation types for recovery of the claimed circuit.
The IOI measurements compare control outcomes, not the claimed circuit's faithfulness or completeness under different circuit-evaluation choices.
IOI prompts include paired ABBA/BABA templates, but results are not reported by prompt variant and do not test whether the same circuit carries IOI across variants or more names.
